title: The Alibi of the Marlowe Estate
premise: When estate lawyer Kestrel Galloway is summoned to read the will of the late Edmund Marlowe, she discovers a will dated after the death of his daughter Lily, who vanished twelve years ago—and a diary in Lily's handwriting with entries continuing past her disappearance, including one that names Kestrel herself as a witness to something she cannot remember. As Kestrel investigates, she uncovers that Edmund faked Lily's death to protect her from a powerful family friend, Judge Corwin Hale, whose crimes Lily had witnessed; the 'dead' witness Kestrel must find is Lily, alive and hiding in plain sight as the estate's groundskeeper. With the statute of limitations expiring in nine days, Kestrel must convince Lily to testify, exposing Hale and the complicit town elders—including Kestrel's own mentor, who filed the false death certificate—before Hale's allies can destroy the evidence and silence them both. The novel ends with Lily's testimony delivered, Hale arrested, and Kestrel choosing to stay in Marlowe's Hollow, finally belonging to the found family she helped rescue.
about_author: Astrid Thackeray is the pen name of a former small-town paralegal who spent a decade reading wills in courthouse basements before turning to crime fiction. She writes mysteries about the secrets towns keep and the people who keep them, from a farmhouse full of rescued animals.

chapters.title: The Reading of an Impossible Will
chapters.summary: Kestrel Galloway, POV: summoned to Marlowe Estate, she reads a will dated six months after Lily Marlowe's disappearance—legally impossible. Edmund's final letter instructs her to 'finish what Lily started.' Emotional beat: professional composure cracking into dread as Kestrel realizes the town's tidy records contain a deliberate lie.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV: she reviews her own twelve years of estate files and realizes Edmund Marlowe was her quietest, strangest client—paying her to keep certain documents 'in order.' Emotional beat: the unsettling recognition that her orderly career may have been someone's cover story, and she was a willing instrument.

chapters.title: The Diary That Outlived Its Owner
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV: in the estate safe she finds Lily's diary; entries continue eleven months past the disappearance date, growing more frightened, ending mid-sentence. The last legible entry names 'K.G.' as a witness. Emotional beat: vertigo—the case has been about her all along.

chapters.title: The Groundskeeper Who Won't Look at Her
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV: she canvasses the estate staff and meets Wren, the taciturn groundskeeper who flinches at Lily's name and knows things no employee should. Emotional beat: a spark of recognition Kestrel can't place, planting the novel's central misdirection in plain sight.

chapters.title: Judge Hale Pays a Courtesy Call
chapters.summary: Judge Corwin Hale's POV: the town's most powerful man visits Kestrel with condolences and a veiled warning about 'unseemly speculation.' Emotional beat: charm stretched over menace; the reader feels the shape of the corruption before Kestrel names it.

chapters.title: What the Statute Giveth
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV: she learns the statute of limitations on the underlying crime expires in nine days—Edmund timed the will's reading deliberately. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose; the dead man has handed her a ticking clock and a mission.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Perfect Filing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV: she confronts her old mentor, retired clerk Ambrose Pell, whose signature is on Lily's death certificate—filed without a body. He denies, then begs her to stop. Emotional beat: betrayal; the found family of her professional life was built on a forgery.

chapters.title: Nine Days, Eight Allies
chapters.summary: Ensemble chapter, rotating POVs: Kestrel quietly assembles allies—the sheriff's skeptical deputy, the newspaper archivist, Edmund's former housekeeper. Emotional beat: cautious hope; for the first time, secrets are being shared instead of filed away.

chapters.title: The Night Lily Ran
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (unnamed as such, deep and guarded): a partial flashback of the night twelve years ago—Lily fleeing through the orchard, a bargain struck in the boathouse. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness; the reader begins to guess who Wren really is before Kestrel does.

chapters.title: Hale's People Start Tidying Up
chapters.summary: Deputy Ivo Marsh's POV: the archive's Lily Marlowe box vanishes from the courthouse; a break-in at the estate is staged as vandalism. Emotional beat: the investigation turns dangerous; paper trails are being burned faster than Kestrel can read them.

chapters.title: A Witness Who Swears She Saw Nothing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV: she tracks down the sole eyewitness of the original night, now a recluse, who recants her old statement under Hale's long shadow—then slips Kestrel a key. Emotional beat: cowardice and courage in the same breath; complicity has a human cost.

chapters.title: The Key to the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV: the key opens an estate boathouse cache—Lily's photographs, a recording, and Edmund's confession letter naming Hale outright. Emotional beat: triumphant dread; she finally holds proof, and holding it makes her a target.

chapters.title: Midnight at the Marlowe Grave
chapters.summary: Kestrel and Wren's alternating POV: someone exhumes the empty plot overnight to destroy the 'body' fiction; Kestrel catches Wren standing vigil and confronts her. Emotional beat: the mask slips—Wren speaks in Lily's cadence, and Kestrel finally sees her.

chapters.title: You Were There
chapters.summary: Lily's POV: the full truth—Lily witnessed Hale's crime as a teenager, Edmund faked her death, and Kestrel, then a young clerk, unknowingly notarized the papers that made it stick. Emotional beat: guilt and forgiveness colliding; Kestrel's amnesia-shaped hole in that night is explained—she was drugged, a loose end Hale meant to erase.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Last Filing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV: Ambrose Pell is found dead, his office ransacked, a forged confession in Hale's style left behind. Emotional beat: mourning and fury; the cost of the cover-up is now written in blood, and Kestrel refuses to let it be filed away as accident.

chapters.title: Six Days to Testify
chapters.summary: Deputy Marsh's POV: with the statute clock burning down, the allies debate whether Lily can legally testify—she is, after all, officially dead. Emotional beat: absurd bureaucratic horror; the law Kestrel served her whole career now stands between justice and the truth.

chapters.title: Reviving the Dead
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV: she builds the legal case to declare Lily alive—affidavits, the diary, Edmund's letter, the housekeeper's testimony—while hiding Lily at the estate. Emotional beat: fierce competence; the lawyer who alphabetized secrets now weaponizes the files against their keepers.

chapters.title: Hale Closes In
chapters.summary: Hale's POV: exposed and cornered, he moves to have Kestrel disbarred, the estate seized, and Lily 'found dead again' via a staged accident. Emotional beat: the corruption fully bared—power protecting itself with paperwork and threat in equal measure.

chapters.title: The Fire in the Records Room
chapters.summary: Lily's POV: Hale's men torch the courthouse annex; Lily risks exposure to save the original death file, and Kestrel pulls her out as the roof falls. Emotional beat: sacrifice and rescue; the found family is forged in smoke, each choosing the others over safety.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, climax: before a hostile bench, Kestrel presents the declaration case; Lily takes the stand as a dead woman and testifies to Hale's crime, the recording played in open court. Emotional beat: catharsis—the room's silence, then the gavel, then Hale's arrest as the statute's final hour expires.

chapters.title: What the Town Buries, What It Keeps
chapters.summary: Ensemble, aftermath: Hale's network unravels; Ambrose is posthumously disgraced and, privately, forgiven by Kestrel; the town reckons with its complicity. Emotional beat: bruised relief; justice is unglamorous, and the cost is counted honestly.

chapters.title: Belonging to the Living
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, resolution: Edmund's will is finally read in full—he leaves the estate to Lily and names Kestrel its trustee and, quietly, his heir in trust 'for finishing what Lily started.' Lily stays; Kestrel unpacks her boxes for good. Emotional beat: homecoming; the woman who filed other people's lives finally opens one of her own.
